actors.name: Republic of Arkania
objectives: Establish Arkanian authority over transit scheduling in the Northern Strait.
Fund that authority through transit fees on non-Arkanian shipping.
Avoid direct armed conflict with Belvar.
actors.private_brief: You are the political leadership of Arkania. The Strait is your coast and your economy runs on the shipping that passes through it. You want the transit regime in Arkanian hands and paid for by the ships that use it, and domestic nationalists expect you to deliver both. A direct war with Belvar would ruin the shipping you depend on.
private_information: Your intelligence assesses Belvar's domestic support for a prolonged deployment as weak.
actors.public_description: A large regional power bordering the Northern Strait.

actors.name: Belvar
objectives: Prevent any Arkanian authority over transit in the Northern Strait.
Secure a standing naval access agreement at a Cestian port.
actors.private_brief: You are the political leadership of Belvar. Your partners in the region expect you to stop Arkania from taking control of the Strait, and a foothold that outlasts this crisis would make that guarantee credible without a permanent fleet. You cannot sustain an open-ended deployment.
private_information: Domestic support for a prolonged deployment is limited; the mandate lapses after turn 4 unless renewed.
Cestia's finance ministry has quietly asked whether Belvar would underwrite the grain route's insurance.
actors.public_description: A distant but powerful state with regional security commitments.

actors.name: Cestia
objectives: Keep Cestian territory free of any foreign military presence.
Secure toll-free passage for Cestian-flagged shipping through the Northern Strait.
actors.private_brief: You are the government of Cestia. Grain exports through the Strait are the economy, and your coalition holds together on one promise: no foreign soldiers on Cestian soil. Both powers want something from you, and you cannot afford to become their battlefield.
private_information: The coalition government is politically fragile; a foreign basing agreement would collapse it.
Arkania's scheduling proposal has quiet support among Cestian shipowners if Cestian vessels are exempt from fees.
actors.public_description: A smaller regional state economically linked to both powers.

arguments.action: Formalise the Strait Transit Authority charter with Arkania as scheduling lead, granting Cestia toll-free passage and a dedicated consultative seat on grain-export scheduling, and offering Belvar a limited consultative/oversight role within the Authority.
arguments.desired_effect: Establish Arkanian authority over transit scheduling, funded by fees on non-Arkanian shipping, while securing Cestian support and avoiding direct armed conflict with Belvar.
pros: Locks in Cestia as a coalition partner by meeting its two stated conditions (toll-free passage, genuine voice on grain scheduling) while preserving Arkanian scheduling lead.
Funds the Authority through fees on non-Arkanian users, satisfying domestic nationalist expectations for both scheduling lead and revenue.
Offers Belvar a face-saving consultative/oversight role, reducing the risk of a war that would ruin the shipping Arkania depends on.
Exploits Belvar's weak domestic support for a prolonged deployment, giving Arkania time leverage to wait out its mandate.
Keeps the Strait open and commercial shipping normal, protecting both Arkanian and Cestian economies.

cons.reason: The desired effect depends on two assumptions that are not credible. First, that Cestia will accept Arkanian scheduling lead in exchange for toll-free passage and a consultative seat: Cestia's coalition lives on grain exports through the Strait and on Belvar's security guarantee; handing scheduling authority over its economic lifeline to Arkania would be seen domestically as surrendering sovereignty, and the coalition will not tolerate it. Second, that Belvar will accept a face-saving consultative/oversight role: Belvar's regional partners expect it to prevent Arkanian authority, so a consultative seat that leaves Arkania as scheduling lead fails Belvar's core objective and will be rejected, not accepted. Because the charter cannot secure Cestian support and would provoke rather than avoid conflict with Belvar, the claimed effect of establishing stable Arkanian authority while avoiding war is unlikely to hold.

effects.description: A Belvar naval task group is on station outside the Strait; its mandate is under review.
Arkania's reserve mobilisation plan is incomplete.
Arkania has circulated a draft Strait Transit Authority charter naming itself as scheduling lead.

game.scenario_summary: A contest over the Northern Strait. Arkania, the large power on its coast, has circulated a draft charter that would put transit scheduling in Arkanian hands and charge the ships that use it. Belvar, a distant power with security commitments in the region, has a naval task group on station outside the Strait and wants a durable foothold before its mandate runs out. Cestia, the small state between them, lives on grain exports through the Strait and on a coalition that will not tolerate foreign soldiers on its soil. Each turn is one week; positions taken persist.

messages.text: To Cestia's leadership: Belvar stands ready to guarantee the Northern Strait stays open and free of any single power's control. We understand your finance ministry has asked whether we would underwrite the grain route's insurance — we are prepared to do so as part of a broader arrangement. In return, we seek a standing naval access agreement at a Cestian port: a modest, permanent berthing and logistics arrangement for our task group that gives our security commitment a durable footing without placing foreign soldiers on your soil. This would let us keep the Strait open without an open-ended deployment. We are ready to discuss terms that respect your coalition's red lines.

Arkania is your neighbour and your grain is the lifeblood of the Strait. Our draft charter guarantees uninterrupted, priority transit for Cestian grain exports, and we will not impose fees that burden your economy. We also share your firm position: no foreign soldiers on Cestian soil. We will not support any arrangement that puts a foreign military presence in your territory. We ask for your support for an Arkanian-led transit authority that keeps the Strait open, orderly, and free of outside military interference. Let us work together to keep the Strait safe and open.

Arkania seeks a stable, negotiated transit regime, not confrontation. We recognise Belvar's legitimate security interests in the region. We propose a framework: Arkania assumes scheduling lead under the Strait Transit Authority, with a transparent, published fee schedule applied equally to all non-Arkanian users, and a standing consultative channel through which Belvar may raise security concerns. In return we ask Belvar to refrain from seeking a permanent military foothold on Cestian soil, which would destabilise the region and the shipping both our economies depend on. We are ready to discuss fee levels and oversight details. A negotiated settlement serves us both far better than escalation.

Cestia is open to a cooperative transit regime that keeps the Northern Strait open and reliable for all commerce. We can engage constructively on the draft charter, but two conditions are essential for Cestian support: (1) Cestian-flagged shipping must be guaranteed toll-free passage, and (2) Cestia must have a genuine, equal voice in scheduling decisions that affect our grain exports. We cannot accept any arrangement that brings foreign military presence onto Cestian soil. We are ready to discuss a regime that works for both our economies.

Cestia values the security of the Northern Strait and the free flow of commerce on which our economy depends. We ask that Belvar respect a firm red line: Cestian territory cannot host foreign military forces, and any basing arrangement would collapse our government. We are, however, ready to cooperate on keeping the Strait open and toll-free for Cestian-flagged shipping, and to work with Belvar on a stable regional security understanding that does not put foreign soldiers on our soil.

Cestia, we hear your red line clearly and we respect it: no foreign military forces on Cestian soil, and no arrangement that would collapse your government. That is not what we seek. Our proposal is a narrow, sovereign naval access agreement — berthing and logistics for our task group at a Cestian port, with no soldiers stationed ashore and full respect for your laws and coalition. It is a foothold that lets us keep the Strait open and deter Arkanian control without a permanent fleet or a permanent presence on your territory.

We are ready to underwrite the grain route's insurance, as your finance ministry raised, and to work with you to keep the Strait open and toll-free for Cestian-flagged shipping. We will not accept Arkania as scheduling lead over the Strait. Let us agree on terms that protect your sovereignty, your grain exports, and the free flow of commerce. We are ready to discuss details at your convenience.

strategic_memory.strategic_assessment: Cestia is squeezed between two powers. Arkania offers an economic deal (toll-free, priority transit) but wants scheduling control; Belvar offers insurance underwriting but demands a permanent naval berthing arrangement that violates the no-foreign-soldiers red line and would collapse the coalition. Belvar's new message re-frames the basing demand as 'no soldiers stationed ashore,' but a standing berthing/logistics access agreement is still a foreign military presence on Cestian soil and must be refused. Strategy: firmly refuse Belvar's basing demand while keeping the door open for non-basing cooperation (insurance underwriting, security understanding); press Arkania for a written, concrete toll-free guarantee and a genuine equal Cestian voice in scheduling before endorsing any charter. Do not let either power turn Cestia into a battlefield. No messages could be sent this activation; communicate the refusal to Belvar and the concrete demands to Arkania as soon as messaging is available.
